title: Reality Bridge
tagline: Privacy-preserving citizen data layer bridging recorded stats & lived reality using EAS & World ID.
description:
Socioeconomic circumstances can shift rapidly due to economic shocks, employment changes, or health events, but official welfare and statistical databases ("Recorded Reality") often take years to update. This creates a critical gap between recorded data and citizens' actual circumstances ("Lived Reality").

Reality Bridge is a privacy-preserving citizen data-quality layer that empowers citizens to report changes in their socioeconomic status and generate verifiable on-chain proof without exposing sensitive personal information.

Key Features & Workflow:
1. Unique Human Verification: Integrates World ID to prevent duplicate submissions while preserving participant anonymity.
2. Cryptographic Commitments: Sensitive household data remains strictly off-chain. A salted SHA-256 cryptographic commitment binds the submission on the client side, producing a downloadable JSON receipt.
3. On-Chain Attestation: Uses Ethereum Attestation Service (EAS) to log lightweight attestations containing only the commitment hash, schema version, region code, and a privacy-preserving "Reality Signal" (classified as LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH severity based on directional indicators).
4. Public Observatory: Displays aggregated, real-time insights, category trends, and regional distributions without revealing individual household data.

By adhering to the principle: "We don't put citizens' data on-chain; we put proof that their voice was counted," Reality Bridge provides a verifiable, citizen-controlled bridge to improve public data quality and social safety net responsiveness.
how_its_made:
Reality Bridge was built using Next.js (App Router, React 19), Tailwind CSS, Wagmi/Viem, and Recharts, combined with privacy and Web3 primitives to create a secure citizen data layer.

Technologies & Partner Integration:

1. World ID Integration (@worldcoin/idkit):
Used for Sybil resistance and Proof of Personhood. World ID ensures each unique human can submit socioeconomic data signals without linking their on-chain wallet address to their real-world identity.

2. Ethereum Attestation Service (EAS):
On-chain attestations are generated using @ethereum-attestation-service/eas-sdk. The schema records non-sensitive metadata: the salted commitment hash, signal level (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH), schema version, region code, and timestamp.

3. Client-Side Zero-Knowledge Privacy & Canonical Cryptography:
All sensitive responses remain strictly on the user's browser. We use the Web Crypto API (crypto.subtle) to canonicalize JSON payloads with sorted keys, append a 32-byte cryptographically secure random nonce, and generate a SHA-256 commitment hash. The raw data is saved directly to the user's device as a downloadable JSON receipt.

4. Viem-to-Ethers Adapter:
Because the EAS SDK expects an Ethers.js signer while Wagmi v3 uses Viem WalletClients, we built a lightweight client-side bridge (walletClientToSigner) that maps Viem transports directly to Ethers JsonRpcSigner interfaces without requiring a heavy full Ethers setup.

5. AI Agent Engineering with Matt Pocock Skills:
Development and codebase architecture were designed and refined using Matt Pocock's Agent Skills framework (mattpocock/skills). We leveraged TDD (Test-Driven Development with Vitest), domain-driven modeling, deep-module architecture, and strict TypeScript patterns to ensure rapid, clean, and verifiable implementation.

6. Dynamic Observatory & Heuristic Engine:
We designed an illustrative Weighted Severity Scoring algorithm across six weighted domains (employment=3, housing=2, health=1, etc.). The Observatory operates on a pre-seeded synthetic dataset of 2,500 records and dynamically injects new user attestations in real time using client-side immutable state reducers.
auto_summary: A Next.js app that lets users submit private socioeconomic change signals and records hashed attestations on-chain for public aggregation.
